task: Add an opt-in NetworkPolicy template to charts/nfs-quota-agent

events.summary: Task brief: add an opt-in NetworkPolicy template to the Helm chart in this worktree (branch feat/chart-networkpolicy). Rendered only when networkPolicy.enabled (default false). Ingress allows metrics port and webUI port when enabled, with optional from selectors. Egress allows DNS (UDP/TCP 53) and Kubernetes API server (apiServer cidr/port list, default allow all).

Scoped strictly to charts/nfs-quota-agent/templates/networkpolicy.yaml, charts/nfs-quota-agent/values.yaml, README.md, README-ko.md, and evaluation trace. Deliberately NOT touched: Go code, RBAC/ClusterRole or privileged settings, Chart.yaml version (per instructions).

Before this change, charts/nfs-quota-agent provided no NetworkPolicy template, requiring operators in policy-enforcing clusters to write custom network isolation manifests manually. Running helm template with networkPolicy flags produced no NetworkPolicy resource.

Review pass (separate context from the authoring lane) found two defects in the drafted templates/networkpolicy.yaml: (1) dead hasKey fallback branches probing metrics.port/ui.port/ui.enabled/enableUI, none of which exist anywhere in this chart's values.yaml or any other template; (2) ingress ports were matched by literal number copied from service.port/service.uiPort, which would silently diverge from the pod's actual listening port if config.metricsAddr or webUI.addr is ever set to a non-default port without also updating service.port/uiPort. Fixed by matching NetworkPolicy ingress ports by the daemonset's named container ports (metrics/http) instead, which removed the need for the fallback branches entirely. Also trimmed the egress.apiServer range from an untested/undocumented multi-shape parser (map without ports/to, .to, .except, bare-string CIDR) down to the single {cidr, port} shape that values.yaml actually documents. podSelector uses chart selectorLabels (matches service.yaml/servicemonitor.yaml); policyTypes includes Egress only when networkPolicy.egress.enabled; networkPolicy.enabled defaults to false. Updated values.yaml's ingress comment to describe the corrected container-port-name matching. Updated values.yaml and README/README-ko documentation.

helm lint ./charts/nfs-quota-agent passed (0 errors, 1 informational icon-recommended notice). helm template ./charts/nfs-quota-agent | grep -c 'kind: NetworkPolicy' returned 0, confirming the template is opt-in. helm template --set networkPolicy.enabled=true (all other networkPolicy/webUI values left at default) rendered a NetworkPolicy with policyTypes: [Ingress] only and a single ingress rule on named port 'metrics', no ingress.from, no egress block. helm template --set networkPolicy.enabled=true --set networkPolicy.egress.enabled=true --set 'networkPolicy.ingress.from[0].namespaceSelector.matchLabels.name=monitoring' --set 'networkPolicy.egress.apiServer[0].cidr=10.96.0.1/32' --set 'networkPolicy.egress.apiServer[0].port=443' --set webUI.enabled=true rendered policyTypes: [Ingress, Egress], ingress rules on named ports 'metrics' and 'http' both scoped to the namespaceSelector, and an egress block with the DNS UDP/TCP 53 rule plus a to: ipBlock cidr 10.96.0.1/32 ports: 443/TCP rule (no allow-all {} fallback, since apiServer was non-empty). python3 .agents/evals/evaluate.py .agents/evals/traces/2026-09-chart-networkpolicy.json returned scorePercent 100.0, 5/5 passed, 0 failed.
events.scope: Helm chart linting and template rendering across default (disabled), enabled-with-defaults, and fully-configured (ingress.from + egress + apiServer + webUI) configurations.
